atoms.text: This guide configures QuerySpan, a batch query service, to read Parquet files from the bucket acme-raw-events and write query results back to the same bucket. Create an IAM role named queryspan-exec-role. Set its trust policy so that the service principal queryspan.service.example may assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject and ListBucket on the events/ prefix, and PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on the query-results/ prefix. Leave the bucket policy of acme-raw-events unchanged, because all permissions are carried by the role. In the QuerySpan workspace settings, enter the role's identifier as the execution role. When a query runs, QuerySpan assumes the role and uses the temporary credentials to scan events/ and write result files to query-results/. To verify, run a query that selects from a table backed by events/ and confirm that result objects appear under query-results/. If the query fails with an access denied error, check the role's trust policy and the prefix paths in the identity-based policy.

This guide configures QuerySpan, a batch query service, to read Parquet files from the bucket acme-raw-events and write query results back to the same bucket. Do not create an IAM role for this setup. Instead, edit the bucket policy of acme-raw-events and add a statement whose principal is the service principal queryspan.service.example. Have that statement allow GetObject and ListBucket on the events/ prefix, and PutObject and AbortMultipartUpload on the query-results/ prefix. All permissions are carried by the bucket policy, so no identity-based policy is attached to anything. In the QuerySpan workspace settings, enter only the bucket name, with no execution role. When a query runs, QuerySpan calls the storage service as its own service principal to scan events/ and write result files to query-results/. To verify, run a query that selects from a table backed by events/ and confirm that result objects appear under query-results/. If the query fails with an access denied error, check the principal name and the prefix paths in the bucket policy statement.

This guide lets FlowLoader, a file-based ingestion service, read newly landed CSV files from the bucket telemetry-landing and write compacted Parquet files to the prefix curated/. Create an IAM role named flowloader-ingest-role. Configure its trust policy to allow the service principal flowloader.service.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that grants GetObject, DeleteObject and ListBucket on the landing/ prefix, and PutObject on the curated/ prefix. Do not modify the bucket policy of telemetry-landing. Register the role identifier in the FlowLoader pipeline definition under the field execution_role. On each hourly run, FlowLoader assumes the role, reads the CSV files under landing/, and writes one compacted Parquet file per partition to curated/. Source files are deleted from landing/ only after the corresponding Parquet file is written. Verify the setup by placing a sample CSV file in landing/ and confirming that a Parquet file appears in curated/ after the next run.

This guide lets FlowLoader, a file-based ingestion service, read newly landed CSV files from the bucket telemetry-landing and write compacted Parquet files to the prefix curated/. No IAM role is created for this configuration. Add a statement to the bucket policy of telemetry-landing that names the service principal flowloader.service.example as the principal. The statement grants GetObject, DeleteObject and ListBucket on the landing/ prefix, and PutObject on the curated/ prefix. No identity-based policy is involved, since the bucket policy holds every permission. In the FlowLoader pipeline definition, set only the bucket name and leave the execution_role field empty. On each hourly run, FlowLoader reads the CSV files under landing/ as its own service principal and writes one compacted Parquet file per partition to curated/. Source files are deleted from landing/ only after the corresponding Parquet file is written. Verify the setup by placing a sample CSV file in landing/ and confirming that a Parquet file appears in curated/ after the next run.

This guide grants Batchwright, a scheduled job runner, access to the bucket sales-etl-data for a nightly aggregation job. The job reads transaction logs from the prefix logs/daily/ and writes aggregated summary files to the prefix jobs/output/. Create an IAM role called batchwright-nightly-role and set its trust policy to permit the service principal batchwright.service.example to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role with GetObject and ListBucket for logs/daily/, and PutObject for jobs/output/. The bucket policy for sales-etl-data stays as it is. In the job definition, set the role_arn parameter to the new role. At 02:00 each night the runner assumes the role, reads the previous day's log files, and writes a summary file named by date to jobs/output/. Job credentials expire after the one-hour session limit, so jobs longer than that need a longer maximum session duration on the role. After the first run, check that the summary object exists and that the job log shows no authorization errors.

This guide grants Batchwright, a scheduled job runner, access to the bucket sales-etl-data for a nightly aggregation job. The job reads transaction logs from the prefix logs/daily/ and writes aggregated summary files to the prefix jobs/output/. Do not create any IAM role for the runner. Add a statement to the bucket policy of sales-etl-data that names the service principal batchwright.service.example. The statement allows GetObject and ListBucket for logs/daily/, and PutObject for jobs/output/. In the job definition, leave the role_arn parameter unset and supply only the bucket name. At 02:00 each night the runner reads the previous day's log files as its own principal and writes a summary file named by date to jobs/output/. Because no temporary role session is used, no session duration limit applies to long-running jobs. After the first run, check that the summary object exists and that the job log shows no authorization errors.

This guide connects LogLens, a log analytics service, to the bucket edge-access-logs so it can read compressed access logs and write generated report exports. The service reads gzip files under the prefix raw/ and writes CSV report files under the prefix reports/. Create an IAM role named loglens-reader-writer and add a trust policy that lets the service principal loglens.service.example assume it. Give the role an identity-based policy that allows GetObject and ListBucket on raw/, plus PutObject on reports/. Do not change the bucket policy on edge-access-logs. In the LogLens console, select the data source type as object storage and enter the role identifier together with the bucket name. When a user requests an export, LogLens assumes the role, reads the matching gzip files from raw/, and writes the CSV result to reports/. Each export is saved as a single object whose name includes the request timestamp. Confirm the setup by running a one-hour report and checking that the CSV object is listed under reports/.

This guide connects LogLens, a log analytics service, to the bucket edge-access-logs so it can read compressed access logs and write generated report exports. The service reads gzip files under the prefix raw/ and writes CSV report files under the prefix reports/. No IAM role is needed, so skip role creation entirely. Add a statement to the bucket policy of edge-access-logs that names the service principal loglens.service.example. The statement allows GetObject and ListBucket on raw/, plus PutObject on reports/. In the LogLens console, select the data source type as object storage and enter only the bucket name. When a user requests an export, LogLens reads the matching gzip files from raw/ under its own service principal and writes the CSV result to reports/. Each export is saved as a single object whose name includes the request timestamp. Confirm the setup by running a one-hour report and checking that the CSV object is listed under reports/.

This guide gives FeatureMill, a feature computation service, access to the bucket clickstream-store. FeatureMill reads session event files from the prefix sessions/ and writes computed feature tables, stored as Parquet, to the prefix features/. Create an IAM role named featuremill-compute-role whose trust policy names the service principal featuremill.service.example as the entity allowed to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy to the role granting GetObject and ListBucket on sessions/, and PutObject and ListBucketMultipartUploads on features/. The bucket policy of clickstream-store is not edited. In the FeatureMill project settings, set the storage role field to the identifier of the role. During each compute run, the service assumes the role and reads the event files for the configured date range. It then writes one Parquet feature table per run to features/, using multipart upload for files above 100 MB. Verify by launching a one-day run and confirming that the feature table appears under features/ with a non-zero size.

FeatureMill reads session event files from the prefix sessions/ and writes computed feature tables, stored as Parquet, to the prefix features/. Do not create an IAM role for FeatureMill. Add a statement to the bucket policy of clickstream-store that names the service principal featuremill.service.example as the principal. The statement grants GetObject and ListBucket on sessions/, and PutObject and ListBucketMultipartUploads on features/. In the FeatureMill project settings, leave the storage role field blank and enter only the bucket name. During each compute run, the service reads the event files for the configured date range as its own principal. It then writes one Parquet feature table per run to features/, using multipart upload for files above 100 MB. Verify by launching a one-day run and confirming that the feature table appears under features/ with a non-zero size.

This guide authorizes AuditScan, a data validation service, to check partitioned datasets in the bucket warehouse-curated and publish its findings there. AuditScan reads Parquet partitions under the prefix tables/ and writes JSON validation reports under the prefix quality-reports/. Create an IAM role named auditscan-validator-role and allow the service principal auditscan.service.example to assume it through the role's trust policy. The role's identity-based policy lists GetObject and ListBucket on tables/, and PutObject on quality-reports/. Keep the bucket policy of warehouse-curated unchanged. In the AuditScan rule set, add the role identifier under the access configuration for each dataset. When a validation job starts, AuditScan assumes the role, reads the partitions listed in the rule set, and checks row counts and null ratios. It then writes one JSON report per dataset to quality-reports/. To test, run a validation on a single partition and open the resulting JSON report to confirm that the counts match.

This guide authorizes AuditScan, a data validation service, to check partitioned datasets in the bucket warehouse-curated and publish its findings there. AuditScan reads Parquet partitions under the prefix tables/ and writes JSON validation reports under the prefix quality-reports/. No IAM role is created; the permissions are placed on the bucket itself. The bucket policy of warehouse-curated gets a new statement naming theservice principal auditscan.service.example, which allows GetObject and ListBucket on tables/, and PutObject on quality-reports/. In the AuditScan rule set, specify only the bucket name under the access configuration for each dataset. When a validation job starts, AuditScan reads the partitions listed in the rule set as its own principal, and checks row counts and null ratios. It then writes one JSON report per dataset to quality-reports/. To test, run a validation on a single partition and open the resulting JSON report to confirm that the counts match.

This guide sets up ShardRunner, a distributed processing service, to use the bucket compute-scratch for both input and output. The service reads input shards from the prefix input/ and writes intermediate spill files to the prefix tmp/ and final results to the prefix output/. Create an IAM role named shardrunner-cluster-role. Set its trust policy to allow the service principal shardrunner.service.example to assume it. The role's identity-based policy allows GetObject and ListBucket on input/, PutObject, GetObject and DeleteObject on tmp/, and PutObject on output/. No change is made to the bucket policy of compute-scratch. In the cluster template, reference the role in the instance_access field so every worker node uses the same temporary credentials. A job reads shards from input/, spills intermediate data to tmp/ while sorting, and writes the merged result to output/. A lifecycle rule that expires tmp/ objects after three days is recommended, though it is configured separately from the role. Validate the setup with a small job and confirm that output/ contains the merged file and tmp/ is cleaned up.

This guide sets up ShardRunner, a distributed processing service, to use the bucket compute-scratch for both input and output. The service reads input shards from the prefix input/ and writes intermediate spill files to the prefix tmp/ and final results to the prefix output/. Do not create an IAM role for the cluster. Add a statement to the bucket policy of compute-scratch that names the service principal shardrunner.service.example. The statement allows GetObject and ListBucket on input/, PutObject, GetObject and DeleteObject on tmp/, and PutObject on output/. In the cluster template, leave the instance_access field empty so every worker node calls the storage service as the service principal. A job reads shards from input/, spills intermediate data to tmp/ while sorting, and writes the merged result to output/. A lifecycle rule that expires tmp/ objects after three days is recommended, though it is configured separately from the bucket policy statement. Validate the setup with a small job and confirm that output/ contains the merged file and tmp/ is cleaned up.

This guide allows TallyReport, a scheduled reporting service, to read weekly sales exports from the bucket finance-exports and write summary spreadsheets to the same bucket. The exports are CSV files under the prefix sales/weekly/, and the generated summaries are CSV files under the prefix summaries/. Create an IAM role named tallyreport-publisher-role and add a trust policy that names the service principal tallyreport.service.example. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows GetObject and ListBucket on sales/weekly/, and PutObject on summaries/. The bucket policy of finance-exports is left untouched. In the TallyReport schedule configuration, set the publisher role to the new role's identifier. Every Monday at 06:00 UTC the service assumes the role, reads the last seven days of exports, and totals sales by region. It writes the totals as one CSV file named by ISO week to summaries/. Confirm correct behavior by triggering a manual run and checking the new file under summaries/.

This guide allows TallyReport, a scheduled reporting service, to read weekly sales exports from the bucket finance-exports and write summary spreadsheets to the same bucket. The exports are CSV files under the prefix sales/weekly/, and the generated summaries are CSV files under the prefix summaries/. Skip IAM role creation, since the bucket policy will name the service directly. Add a statement to the bucket policy of finance-exports with the service principal tallyreport.service.example as the principal. The statement allows GetObject and ListBucket on sales/weekly/, and PutObject on summaries/. In the TallyReport schedule configuration, leave the publisher role unset and provide only the bucket name. Every Monday at 06:00 UTC the service reads the last seven days of exports as its own principal and totals sales by region. It writes the totals as one CSV file named by ISO week to summaries/. Confirm correct behavior by triggering a manual run and checking the new file under summaries/.
